intent: A compact action attached inside an InputGroup's addon, sharing the field's frame.
typical_uses: A clear, copy or reveal action at the end of a field
An icon-only action that has an accessible name (pass aria-label)

dont_use_when.situation: An action beside a field rather than inside its frame, or anywhere outside an InputGroup

invariants.text: With `icon` set and no children the button renders icon-only and carries no accessible name of its own - `aria-label` is required.
A disabled InputGroupButton dims only itself; the group dims as a whole only when its field is disabled.
Inside a group the button is never taller than the group's row, and its focus ring is drawn one border-width out instead of the kit's usual standoff so it stays inside the field's frame.

anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `icon` with no children and an `aria-label`; the button squares itself up at whichever size is active

a11y.by: Base UI's own Button primitive, plus input-group.test.tsx resolving an icon-less button by getByRole('button', { name: 'Clear' }) from its aria-label and asserting its type property is 'button'

icon.states: icon is a React node, not a value
icon.because: `ReactNode` is a union, and the compiler emits one JSON type per property - an element, a string, a fragment and `false` are all valid and only tsc can tell them from a mistake. It is Button's icon slot, reaching this part unchanged.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the button's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the button's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through button.module.css and input-group.module.css, not through this.

good.title: Icon-only clear action
good.code:
<InputGroup>
  <InputGroupInput placeholder="Search" aria-label="Search" />
  <InputGroupAddon align="inline-end">
    <InputGroupButton icon={<XIcon />} aria-label="Clear" onClick={clear} />
  </InputGroupAddon>
</InputGroup>

bad.title: Icon-only size from an older API
bad.why: Icon-only is derived from `icon` with no children, not from a size, and an icon in children misses the slot that sizes it and marks it decorative. Use `icon={<XIcon />}` with an `aria-label`.

icon.description: Partially typed: ReactNode. The compiler emits one JSON type per property and none for this one; shape checked by tsc, see x-uikit.partially_typed_props. icon is a React node, not a value. `ReactNode` is a union, and the compiler emits one JSON type per property - an element, a string, a fragment and `false` are all valid and only tsc can tell them from a mistake. It is Button's icon slot, reaching this part unchanged.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ButtonState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the button's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: ButtonState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the button's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through button.module.css and input-group.module.css, not through this.
